reasoning: The package is a standard binary AUR package for the Xenia Edge Xbox 360 emulator. The PKGBUILD downloads a prebuilt AppImage and license file from the project's official GitHub repository (has207/xenia-edge). The AppImage has a pinned SHA256 checksum, closing the swap risk. The license file uses SKIP, which is acceptable for small, easily verifiable files. All PKGBUILD functions (prepare, build, package) perform standard operations: extracting the AppImage, organizing files, adjusting desktop entries, and installing to /opt with symlinks. No malicious code execution, network exfiltration, or suspicious operations are present. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all three files and found them safe. The other two models had API/parsing errors but their successful reviews of the PKGBUILD also found it safe.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement (inconclusive vs safe) was caused by tool errors, not substantive security concerns. The qwen model failed with HTTP 400 errors when reviewing LICENSE and .SRCINFO. The openrouter model failed to parse the PKGBUILD decision. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. When models successfully reviewed the PKGBUILD, all agreed it was safe with no malicious indicators.
coverage_issues: qwen model: API errors (HTTP 400) prevented review of LICENSE and .SRCINFO files
openrouter model: Failed to parse decision from model response for PKGBUILD review
learnings: Implement retry logic or fallback models when API requests fail with HTTP errors
Add more robust parsing of model responses to handle variations in output format
When multiple models agree on safety for successfully reviewed files, treat tool errors on other files as non-blocking if those files are low-risk (e.g., LICENSE files)
Consider the risk profile of files when deciding if incomplete coverage should block a verdict - license files with SKIP checksums are low-risk
